agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The format is confirmed. I'll build the texts as prompt + the model's own answer. They are the 98 cut answers of the original model (67 from pass 1, 31 from pass 5 original) and, as controls, 150 finished LaTeX-regime answers from pass 1. All of them are original-model texts, scored by the original model, so the token states match what happened in generation. Per text I'll keep the id, kind and prompt, so I can map the loop onset (first repeated line) to a token index afterwards. I'll record the plan in the notes, then send the pass.

The set has 249 texts (98 cut answers and 150 finished LaTeX controls, plus one extra cut answer from the overlap), at most 967 tokens, about 2.8 GB of hidden states, within the 6 GB limit. I'm sending the teacher-forced pass on the original model with hidden states at layers 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24, per-token log-probs and top-20 alternatives. The first thing I'll check afterwards: at each cut answer's loop onset, is a concluding continuation (\boxed, "Therefore", "####", "Final") among the top alternatives with substantial probability? Close runners-up would mean a narrow decision to restart instead of conclude, which is a good target for a component-level fix. Absent conclusion tokens would mean the model has nothing to conclude, and the loops reflect real inability.

The pass ran on the original weights (edited_tensors 0). One thing stands out already: the cut answers have a mean token log-prob of about −0.5 to −0.9, although they were decoded greedily, so the model's next-token distributions are quite flat along those answers. Now the loop onsets. For each cut answer I'll find the first token of the first exactly repeated line. At that token I'll check the greedy (top-1) token's probability, and whether any of the top-20 alternatives is a concluding token (\boxed, "Therefore", "Thus", "So", "####", "Final", "answer"), with its probability. I'll also compare the mean log-prob of cut and finished answers. A decisive restart (p > 0.8) means the loop is a confident habit. A near-tie with a concluding alternative means a narrow decision that a targeted change could tip.

The loop decision is not close. At the onset of repetition the restart token has median probability 0.99 (above 0.8 in 81% of cases), and no concluding token appears among the top-20 alternatives in any of the 89 onsets. Along the answer, cut and finished texts are about equally confident (−0.06 vs −0.05 nat/token). So the loop is a confident, self-reinforcing copy, not a narrowly lost "conclude" decision, and the "suppressed conclusion" hypothesis is refuted. To localise the copy state instead, I'll contrast line-start tokens inside loops with line-start tokens before the onset in the same cut answers, which controls for difficulty. As a position control, I'll use line-starts at comparable positions in finished answers. If a direction separates in-loop from pre-loop line-starts much better than it separates late from early positions in finished answers, it is a loop-specific state that I can trace to the components that write it.
